MIND. [1] [Cham.]
Dulness of senses, diminished power of comprehension.
Child cries ; quiet only when carried.
Piteous moaning of child because he cannot have what he wants.
Whining restlessness ; the child wants this and that, which, when offered, is refused or pushed away.
Averse to talking, short and snappish.
Cannot endure being spoken to, or interrupted while speaking, especially after rising from sleep.
Child does not wish to be touched.
Patient cannot bear any one near him, and answers snappishly.
Peevish disposition, nothing pleases.
Peevish about everything, with dyspnœa.
Peevishness ; she seeks a cause for being peevish at everything ; can't return a civil answer.
Very irritable and fretful ; child must be carried.
Irritable, impatient mood.
Easily chagrined or excited to anger.
The child can only be quieted by carrying it on the arm.
Excessive uneasiness, anxiety, agonizing tossing about, with tearing pains in abdomen.
Oversensitiveness to pain, which seems unbearable and drives to despair.
   

INNER HEAD. [3] [Cham.]
Throbbing headache.
Transient attacks of throbbing in one-half of brain.
One-sided drawing headache.
Congestion to head : following anger ; with pressure while lying down ; on vertex ; with heat in face and oppression of chest ; with stitches in head and chest.
Megrim.
   

OUTER HEAD. [4] [Cham.]
Warm sweat on head, wetting hair.
   

SIGHT AND EYES. [5] [Cham.]
Eyes swollen in morning ; agglutinated with purulent mucus.
Violent pressure in orbital region ; sensation in eyeball, as if it was tightly compressed from all sides, with momentary obstruction of vision.
   

HEARING AND EARS. [6] [Cham.]
Roaring in ears, as from rushing water.
Single large stitches in ear, especially when stooping, with ill humor and peevishness about trifles.
Pressing earache in spells, with tearing pain, extorting cries.
Particularly sensitive to open air about ears.
   

UPPER FACE. [8] [Cham.]
Redness of one cheek, returning in paroxysms, without shivering or internal heat. θ Hemicrania.
Red face, or redness and heat of one (l.) cheek, the other being pale.
One cheek red and hot, the other pale and cold.
Face sweats after eating or drinking.
   

TEETH AND GUMS. [10] [Cham.]
Toothache : stitching ; digging ; gnawing ; from suppressed perspiration ; from taking cold ; during or after eating ; if anything warm is taken into mouth, especially after coffee, < by talking ; in open air ; in room ; getting warm in bed ; during menstruation and pregnancy ; most left side and lower teeth ; < at night ; affecting principally women and children ; after abuse of mercury.
Toothache recommences when entering the warm room, or drinking anything warm.
Teeth feel too long.
Gums red and tender. θ Dentition.
Teething children : with watery, greenish and also chopped diarrhœa, smelling like rotten eggs ; jerking of limbs or starting ; convulsions ; child bends double and draws legs upon abdomen ; moaning ; want to be carried ; dry cough ; restless at night ; want to drink ; quick rattling breathing.
   

TASTE, SPEECH, TONGUE. [11] [Cham.]
Bitter taste in mouth, in morning.
   

INNER MOUTH. [12] [Cham.]
Heat in mouth, pharynx and œsophagus to stomach.
Collection of saliva, of metallic, sweetish taste.
Fetid smell from mouth.
   

PALATE AND THROAT. [13] [Cham.]
Spasmodic constriction of pharynx.
Sore throat, with swelling of parotid or submaxillary glands, or tonsils.

APPETITE, THIRST. DESIRES, AVERSIONS. [14] [Cham.]
Want of appetite.
Great thirst for cold water and desire for acid drinks.
Likes to hold cold water to mouth a long time, when drinking. θ Dentition.
   

EATING AND DRINKING. [15] [Cham.]
After eating and drinking, heat and sweat of face.
Thirsty and hot with the pains.
   

HICCOUGH, BELCHING, NAUSEA AND VOMITING. [16] [Cham.]
Eructations : sour ; constant, empty ; aggravate the pain.
Fruitless efforts to vomit.
   

SCROBICULUM AND STOMACH. [17] [Cham.]
Pressure in stomach, as from a stone pressing down.
Constrictive gastralgia in coffee drinkers.
   

ABDOMEN AND LOINS. [19] [Cham.]
Colic returns from time to time, flatus accumulates in hypochondria, and stitches shoot through chest.
Wind colic, abdomen distended like a drum, wind passes in small quantities without relief ; > by applying warm cloths.
Abdomen tympanitic and sensitive to touch. θ Agalactia. θ Peritonitis.
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Cham.]
Stools : green, slimy, mucous ; mixed green and white, mucous ; chopped, white and yellow, mucous ; green or yellowish ; watery, frequent, preceded by cutting constricting bellyache, < in epigastric region ; mucous, with colic and vomituritio ; bilious, with burning in anus ; painful, thin, green, consisting of feces and mucus ; green, watery, corroding, with colic, thirst, bitter taste and bitter eructations ; like chopped or stirred eggs, smelling sour ; hot, smelling like rotten eggs ; changeable ; containing undigested food ; mucous and bloody.
Constipation from inactivity of anus.
Ulcerating fissures at anus.
   

FEMALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [23] [Cham.]
Menstrual colic, following anger.
Membranous dysmenorrhœa.
Yellow, smarting leucorrhœa.
   

PREGNANCY. PARTURITION. LACTATION. [24] [Cham.]
Labor pain press upward ; she is hot and thirsty, cross and inclined to scold.
Rigidity of os ; scarcely able to endure the pains.
After pains very acute and distressing.
Puerperal convulsions, after anger ; or has one red cheek, the other being pale.
Mamma hard and tender to touch, with drawing pains ; is fretful, sleepless and cross.
Children have spasms in consequence of nursing milk vitiated by a fit of anger.
   

VOICE AND LARYNX. TRACHEA AND BRONCHIA. [25] [Cham.]
Sensation of rawness and scraping in larynx.
Tickling in pit of throat causing scraping, dry cough.
   

RESPIRATION. [26] [Cham.]
Suffocative attacks from repercussion of measles eruption, by taking cold.
Asthma after a fit of anger.
   

COUGH. [27] [Cham.]
Scraping, dry cough, caused by tickling in pit of throat, < at night, even in sleep, especially with children after taking cold in winter.
   

UPPER LIMBS. [32] [Cham.]
Arms immediately go to sleep, if she grasps anything firmly ; she is obliged to let them sink down.
   

LOWER LIMBS. [33] [Cham.]
Cramp in legs and calves.
Burning of soles, at night ; puts feet out of bed.
   

LIMBS IN GENERAL. [34] [Cham.]
Violent rheumatic pains drive him out of bed at night, and compel him to walk about.
   

REST. POSITION. MOTION. [35] [Cham.]
Child gets relief from being carried.
   

NERVES. [36] [Cham.]
Oversensitiveness after abuse of coffee or opium.
Child suddenly stiffens body and bends backwards, kicks when carried, screams immoderately and throws everything off. θ Dentition.
   

SLEEP. [37] [Cham.]
Sleepy, but cannot sleep.
Sleepless and restless at night.
   

TEMPERATURE AND WEATHER. [39] [Cham.]
Pains are aggravated by heat.
Oversensitive to open air, aversion to wind, particularly sensitive about ears.
   

FEVER. [40] [Cham.]
Chill and coldness of whole body, with burning heat of face and hot breath.
Heat and shivering intermingled, mostly with one red and one pale cheek.
Long-lasting heat, with violent thirst and frequent startings in sleep.
Hot and thirsty with the pains.
Profuse sweat of covered parts.
Sweat during sleep, most on head, usually sour smelling.
   

ATTACKS, PERIODICITY. [41] [Cham.]
Pains recur in evening and are worse before midnight.
   

SENSATIONS. [43] [Cham.]
Oversensitiveness of senses, especially if produced by coffee or narcotics.
Paralytic sensations are always accompanied by drawing or tearing pain, and drawing or tearing pains rarely occur without paralytic or numb sensation in the part.
   

TISSUES. [44] [Cham.]
Digestive canal : increased and altered secretions, accumulation of flatus during the period of dentition.
Looseness of bowels, with colic, following anger, or in children.
   

TOUCH. PASSIVE MOTION. INJURIES. [45] [Cham.]
Children obtain relief by being carried.
   

SKIN. [46] [Cham.]
Skin moist and burning hot.
   

STAGE OF LIFE, CONSTITUTION. [47] [Cham.]
Light or brown hair, nervous, excitable temperament.
Children, newborn and during period of dentition.
Adults, even aged persons with arthritic or rheumatic diathesis.
